mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which raises discount rates for equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of cases when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 3% each over three months signal broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 3% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 6.0% y/y), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as markets price prolonged monetary tightening.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when CPIAUCSL > 6.0% and FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (base 2017=100) indicates weakening real economic activity, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 5% over three months signals housing market weakness, reducing consumer confidence and business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when HOUST falls > 5% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), a strong payroll gain (PAYEMS > 100k) signals labor market overheating, prompting aggressive monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 100k, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 0.5% q/q) indicates economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 0.5% q/q, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.
